title: PLAYER 2 TAKING OVER THE RAID DOES NOT LIGHT THE FIRES TWICE
why: Cloud robustness hunt. A linked player 2 window plans no fires of its own: it keeps the host fires from the world word. When the host window goes and player 2 picks up the raid (his ruling), that window plans its fires for the first time and lit at once every planned fire whose time had passed, on top of the host fires it already holds, so a fire the host had lit stood twice on the same spot (twice the burn) and others could appear all at once. Proven in two real headless windows on v27.27 (2 player DEMO, seed 23): 124 s in, player 2 held one lit fire at 193,2829; the host window closed and 2 s later player 2 held two fires at 193,2829. Now a window that took over marks the plan entries already due as done when it first plans, so it keeps the host fires and lights only the ones still to come. A raid that never had a host is unchanged.
now: When player 1 leaves mid-raid and player 2 carries on, the fires already burning are not lit a second time.

edits.replacement: if(!S.fplan){ firePlan(S); if(G.netWasJoin){ for(i=0;i<S.fplan.length;i++) if(t>=S.fplan[i].at) S.fplan[i].on=1; } }   // v27.xx (cloud-robust-takeover-fires), CLOUD HUNT 2026-10-15: a window that took the raid over keeps the host fires it holds, so the plan entries already due are done
